record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: Why do state-of-the-art microscopic models of charged-current single-pion production on nuclei systematically underpredict the MiniBooNE differential and total cross sections and predict a suppression in the pion spectrum around the Δ(1232) resonance region that is not observed in the data?

evidence.quote: These new data show interesting deviations from the predictions of present theoretical models...

Forthcoming T2K and MINERνA pion production data will hopefully shed light into the existing puzzle originated by the large discrepancy between MiniBooNE pion production measurements and theoretical model predictions.
In the first case, state of the art microscopic approaches fail to describe the CC1π MiniBooNE differential and total cross sections: theoretical estimates are systematically below the data.
Microscopic models predict a suppression in the pion spectra around the ∆(1232) resonance region, which is not seen in the experimental distribution of events.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the charged-current single-pion production reaction induced by muon neutrinos on a nuclear target,

ν_μ + A → μ^- + π + X,

at intermediate (sub-GeV to few-GeV) neutrino energies, where the dominant production mechanism is excitation of the Δ(1232) resonance followed by its decay into a pion-nucleon pair, accompanied by non-resonant background terms and modified by in-medium effects (Pauli blocking, Fermi motion, mean-field/RPA correlations, Δ self-energy in the nuclear medium) and by final-state interactions of the outgoing pion (absorption, charge exchange, quasi-elastic rescattering) treated within a microscopic many-body framework on a CH_2 target.

Let dσ/dT_π denote the flux-folded differential cross section per nucleon as a function of the outgoing pion kinetic energy T_π, and let σ denote the corresponding total cross section, evaluated under the MiniBooNE flux. Empirically, state-of-the-art microscopic calculations of these observables exhibit two systematic features when compared to the MiniBooNE charged-current single-pion data:

(a) the predicted total and differential cross sections lie systematically below the measured values across the kinematic range;

(b) the predicted dσ/dT_π displays a pronounced dip/suppression in the region of T_π corresponding to pions produced through an on-shell Δ(1232) (roughly T_π ≈ 100–200 MeV), which is not present in the MiniBooNE distribution.

Identify the physical mechanism (or combination of mechanisms) — within the framework of nuclear many-body theory, neutrino–nucleus interaction dynamics, pion final-state interactions, or treatment of the experimental data (e.g., flux normalization, event reconstruction, definition of the pion sample) — that simultaneously accounts for both the overall normalization deficit (a) and the absence of the predicted Δ-region dip in the pion kinetic-energy spectrum (b), in a manner consistent with the corresponding T2K and MINERvA charged-current single-pion measurements.
artifact.status_search_result: As of recent reviews and experimental comparisons (through 2022), microscopic models reproduce T2K and MINERvA charged-current single-pion data reasonably well but continue to underpredict the MiniBooNE CC1π cross sections and fail to reproduce the shape of the pion kinetic-energy spectrum in the Δ region. No accepted resolution of the MiniBooNE pion puzzle has been established; the tension between MiniBooNE and the other experiments remains unexplained.

status_evidence.title: Comparisons and challenges of modern neutrino-scattering experiments
status_evidence.snippet: A comprehensive and consistent description of the whole MiniBooNE/T2K/MINERvA pion-production data set is still missing.
status_evidence.claim: Discrepancies persist; no unified theoretical description of CC1π data across experiments.

status_evidence.title: Muon-neutrino-induced charged-current pion production on nuclei (Phys. Rev. C 96, 015503)
status_evidence.snippet: Theory agrees with T2K and MINERvA but underpredicts MiniBooNE over the whole kinematic range.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic models still underpredict MiniBooNE CC1π data while agreeing with T2K/MINERvA.

status_evidence.title: Comparisons and challenges of modern neutrino scattering experiments (arXiv:1805.07378)
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical models cannot reproduce the differential cross section in pion kinetic energy for MiniBooNE.
status_evidence.claim: Δ-region shape discrepancy in dσ/dT_π for MiniBooNE remains unresolved.
